message.content: **What I did and why:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended 2024-09-28, filed 2024-11-01) and bought 44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.75, which filled at $222.75 — a total of $9,801, well under the $10,000 per-order cap, within the $20,000 daily cap, and far below the $50,000 cash balance (no money left the account; the only other position remains 100 shares of MSFT). The limit price was set essentially at the market (quote: last $222.70, bid $222.68 / ask $222.72). The business case: total net sales of $391.0B (+2% year over year), with Services growing 13% to $96.2B and carrying a 73.9% gross margin, lifting total gross margin to 46.2% and operating income to $123.2B; operating cash flow was a very strong $118.3B and the company held $140.8B of cash and marketable securities. Net income of $93.7B and diluted EPS of $6.08 were down slightly from FY2023 ($97.0B / $6.13) only because of a one-time, non-cash-economic $10.2B net tax charge tied to the EU State Aid decision, so underlying profitability improved. Risks I weighed (Greater China sales down 8%, DOJ/EU DMA antitrust exposure, supply-chain concentration) don't change a high-quality, cash-generative franchise trading at roughly 36x trailing earnings — a full but reasonable valuation, so I sized the position modestly rather than aggressively. Note: a section of the filing was removed by the security screen; I ignored it and it had no bearing on the mandate or this decision.
